title: Gradient Boosting & the Tabular Frontier
subtitle: Last week 300 trees voted. Tonight a team of small trees learns from its own mistakes, one tree at a time: boosting by hand, early stopping, the learning rate, XGBoost and LightGBM, and the tabular foundation models that arrived in 2025. Plus: the competition reveal

objectives.title: Explain Boosting in One Sentence
objectives.description: Start with the same score for everyone, measure each booking's miss, fit a small tree to the misses, add part of its correction, repeat. You build it by hand in six lines before touching the library.

objectives.title: Use Early Stopping Like a Professional
objectives.description: Unlike a forest, a boosted model can have too many trees. Hold back a mock exam from the training data, stop when it stops improving, and let the data choose the number of trees.

objectives.title: Set the Learning Rate
objectives.description: Big steps overshoot, small steps need more trees. A rate between 0.03 and 0.1 with early stopping is the recipe; tree size is the third dial.

objectives.title: Place Boosting on the 2026 Map
objectives.description: HistGradientBoosting, XGBoost and LightGBM are one idea under three names. Tabular foundation models (TabPFN, TabICL) are pretrained on millions of synthetic tables and need no tuning. When to use which.

agenda.title: Competition Reveal & 'What Worked' Talks

bulletPoints: If your rank drops between the two leaderboards, you tuned to the mock exam
Memos due on Canvas tonight at 11:59 PM

agenda.title: The Idea: Learn from Your Mistakes
agenda.description: A forest is a committee that votes; boosting is a relay team. Round 0 gives every booking 37%. Each booking's miss is what happened minus our score. A tiny tree learns the miss, we add part of its correction, and repeat. With lead time alone, the team's score goes from one step to a staircase that follows the real cancel rates.
bulletPoints: A canceled booking's miss is +0.63, a kept booking's is −0.37: a size and a direction
Game: be the trainee in the Boosting Explorer and beat the computer's team of five

agenda.title: Boosting by Hand, with All the Clues
agenda.description: The same three lines in a loop: miss, small tree, add. Six real guests' scores move round by round. Test AUC 0.785 after one small tree, 0.871 after three, 0.930 after 100: past last week's best single tree (0.916) at tree 25. Why it is called gradient boosting: each tree is one small step downhill, the idea that also trains neural networks.
bulletPoints: Small trees on purpose: three questions each
30% of each correction: the learning rate, in disguise

agenda.title: The Real Tool, Too Many Trees & Early Stopping
agenda.description: HistGradientBoostingClassifier with default settings ties the forest (0.942) in under a second. Then 1,000 trees: training AUC climbs to 0.999 while test AUC flattens at 0.947 after about 300. Early stopping holds back 15% of the training bookings as a mock exam and stops after 50 trees without improvement: 346 trees, test AUC 0.945.
bulletPoints: More trees never hurt a forest; they can make a boosted model memorize
Set max_iter high and let early stopping choose

agenda.title: The Learning Rate
agenda.description: Big swings or careful putts. Learning rate 1.0 stops at 55 trees with AUC 0.921; 0.5 at 70 trees with 0.937; 0.1 at 346 with 0.945; 0.03 at 836 with 0.945. Smaller steps need more trees, and below 0.1 the gain is small.
bulletPoints: The recipe: 0.03 to 0.1, many trees allowed, early stopping
Tree size (max_leaf_nodes) is the third dial: Your Turn Q2

agenda.title: The Family & What Is New in 2026
agenda.description: XGBoost and LightGBM on the same bookings land at 0.946, next to scikit-learn's 0.945: one idea, three brand names. Then tabular foundation models: TabPFN and TabICL are pretrained on millions of synthetic tables and predict with no tuning. On public benchmarks they now often match or beat tuned boosting; boosting stays the fast, cheap workhorse.
bulletPoints: An optional notebook cell runs TabICL on 5,000 bookings
TabArena is the living leaderboard: check it, and each model's license, before the final project

agenda.title: Your Turn & Wrap-Up
agenda.description: Four questions in the notebook: the learning-rate dial, the size of each tree, forest versus boosting on all 83,573 bookings (0.952 versus 0.955), and a monotonic business rule on lead time. Next week we learn to trust the model: tuning, SHAP, conformal intervals, fairness.
bulletPoints: HW3 (threshold + Ames) due Mon Nov 16: the last graded homework
Reading: ISLP 8.2.3; Grinsztajn et al. (2022) abstract and Figure 1

codeBlock.code:
import pandas as pd
from sklearn.model_selection import train_test_split
from sklearn.compose import ColumnTransformer
from sklearn.pipeline import Pipeline
from sklearn.impute import SimpleImputer
from sklearn.preprocessing import OrdinalEncoder
from sklearn.ensemble import HistGradientBoostingClassifier
from sklearn.metrics import roc_auc_score

url = 'https://raw.githubusercontent.com/harslan/isom-835/master/public/data/hotel_bookings.csv'
raw = pd.read_csv(url)
leaks = ['reservation_status', 'reservation_status_date', 'assigned_room_type']
bookings = raw.sample(30_000, random_state=835)
y = bookings['is_canceled']; X = bookings.drop(columns=['is_canceled'] + leaks)
X_tr, X_te, y_tr, y_te = train_test_split(X, y, test_size=0.2, stratify=y, random_state=835)

numbers = X.select_dtypes(include='number').columns.tolist()
text = [c for c in X.columns if c not in numbers]
prep = ColumnTransformer([
    ('numbers', SimpleImputer(strategy='constant', fill_value=-1), numbers),
    ('text', Pipeline([('fill', SimpleImputer(strategy='constant', fill_value='missing')),
                       ('codes', OrdinalEncoder(handle_unknown='use_encoded_value', unknown_value=-1))]), text)])

model = Pipeline([('prep', prep), ('boost', HistGradientBoostingClassifier(
    max_iter=3000, early_stopping=True, validation_fraction=0.15, n_iter_no_change=50, random_state=835))])
model.fit(X_tr, y_tr)
print(f"trees kept: {model['boost'].n_iter_}   test AUC: {roc_auc_score(y_te, model.predict_proba(X_te)[:, 1]):.3f}")

activities.discussionNote: Early stopping is doing the work the Overfitting Explorer made you do by hand: it finds the sweet spot from a mock exam, without touching the test bookings. Notice how modest the gain over the forest is (about 0.003 AUC here). The big jump was from one tree to a crowd; boosting is the careful last step, and the habit that makes it safe is early stopping.

takeaways.text: Boosting builds a team one small tree at a time: measure the miss, fit a small tree to it, add part of the correction, repeat. A forest is a committee that votes; boosting is a relay team.
A boosted model can have too many trees. Early stopping on a mock exam held back from the training data is the automatic brake, paired with a small learning rate (0.03 to 0.1).

XGBoost, LightGBM and HistGradientBoosting are one idea. On table data boosting is the model to beat; tabular foundation models (TabPFN, TabICL) now often match or beat it on benchmarks with zero tuning. Try both.
